data.bio:
Anindya founded Lumina Estates in 2014 after a decade advising private clients at an international bank. She leads the Jakarta team and personally handles the agency's landmark residences in Menteng and Kemang.

Clients value her discretion, her command of the South Jakarta market and her network among architects and notaries.

Sekar leads our rental desk, matching diplomatic and corporate tenants with family homes in Kemang, Pondok Indah and Menteng. She knows which streets flood, which schools have waiting lists and which landlords answer the phone.

Her team manages more than 60 leases a year, from the first viewing to the handover inventory.

Rafael has sold more than 120 villas and land parcels across Canggu, Seminyak and Ubud since moving to Bali in 2011. Before real estate he trained as an architect in Surabaya, which shows in the way he reads a plot, a view corridor or a leasehold contract.

He advises overseas buyers on the right ownership structure (PT PMA, leasehold or Hak Pakai) and works with a trusted circle of notaries in Badung and Gianyar.

Maarten moved from Amsterdam to Ubud in 2016 and has helped European families relocate to Bali ever since. He guides buyers through due diligence, building permits (PBG) and the practicalities of life on the island.

He is often the first call for clients looking for a quiet home with a rice-field view.

data.body:
Living in Kemang

Kemang grew from a quiet orchard village into South Jakarta's most international neighbourhood. Low-rise houses with gardens line the side streets off Jalan Kemang Raya, while the main road keeps its cafés, design shops and galleries.

Who lives here

  • Families with children at the Jakarta Intercultural School and nearby international schools

  • Diplomats and corporate leaders who prefer a house to a tower

  • Architects, designers and restaurateurs

Expect traffic at school hours and plan around the rainy season: we can tell you which streets stay dry.
data.intro: Leafy, cosmopolitan and walkable by Jakarta standards, Kemang is where expatriate families and creative professionals settle for its international schools, galleries and garden houses.

highlights.text: JIS Pattimura and several British and French schools within 15 minutes.
highlights.label: International schools

highlights.text: Rare in Jakarta: detached homes on 600–1,500 m² plots with mature trees.
highlights.label: Garden houses

highlights.text: Galleries, specialty coffee and some of the city's best restaurants on Jalan Kemang Raya.
highlights.label: Dining and culture

data.body:
Tinggal di Kemang

Kemang tumbuh dari desa kebun buah yang tenang menjadi kawasan paling internasional di Jakarta Selatan. Rumah-rumah rendah bertaman berjajar di jalan-jalan samping Jalan Kemang Raya, sementara jalan utamanya dipenuhi kafe, toko desain dan galeri.

Siapa yang tinggal di sini

  • Keluarga dengan anak di Jakarta Intercultural School dan sekolah internasional sekitarnya

  • Diplomat dan pimpinan perusahaan yang lebih memilih rumah daripada apartemen

  • Arsitek, desainer dan pemilik restoran

Perhitungkan kemacetan di jam sekolah dan musim hujan: kami dapat memberi tahu jalan mana yang tetap kering.
data.intro: Rimbun, kosmopolitan dan nyaman untuk berjalan kaki menurut ukuran Jakarta, Kemang menjadi pilihan keluarga ekspatriat dan para profesional kreatif berkat sekolah internasional, galeri dan rumah-rumah bertaman.

highlights.text: JIS Pattimura serta beberapa sekolah Inggris dan Prancis dalam 15 menit.
highlights.label: Sekolah internasional

highlights.text: Langka di Jakarta: rumah tunggal di lahan 600–1.500 m² dengan pohon-pohon besar.
highlights.label: Rumah bertaman

highlights.text: Galeri, kopi spesialti dan beberapa restoran terbaik kota di Jalan Kemang Raya.

data.body:
A heritage address

Planned in the 1910s as Batavia's first garden city, Menteng still has the tree-lined streets, roundabouts and parks of its original design. Many villas are protected heritage buildings, which keeps the neighbourhood's character intact and supply very limited.

What to know before buying

  • Heritage-listed homes need approval for exterior changes

  • Plots are large, often 1,000 m² or more

  • Ten minutes to Sudirman and Thamrin
data.intro: Jakarta's original garden suburb: Dutch-era villas, wide boulevards and parks, a short drive from the central business district.

highlights.text: Art deco and Indies-style homes from the 1920s and 1930s.
highlights.label: Heritage villas

highlights.text: Taman Suropati and Taman Menteng are on the doorstep.
highlights.label: Parks

highlights.text: The business district, embassies and Gondangdia station within minutes.
highlights.label: Central

data.body:
Space for families

Pondok Indah was developed in the 1970s as an upmarket estate and remains one of the most sought-after addresses for families who want space, security and everything close by.

  • Pondok Indah Golf Course and Pondok Indah Hospital

  • Pondok Indah Mall 1, 2 and 3

  • Direct access to the JORR toll road
data.intro: A planned residential estate in South Jakarta with spacious family homes, a championship golf course, hospitals and two large malls.

highlights.text: Homes along the fairways of Pondok Indah Golf Course.
highlights.label: Golf and green

highlights.text: Pondok Indah Hospital, one of Jakarta's best private hospitals.
highlights.label: Healthcare

highlights.text: Toll road access to the airport and the CBD.
highlights.label: Connected

data.body:
From rice fields to beach clubs

Canggu has changed faster than anywhere else in Bali. Rice fields still frame many villas, yet the area now offers co-working spaces, international schools and some of the island's best restaurants.

Areas within Canggu

  • Berawa: lively, close to Finns and Atlas beach clubs

  • Batu Bolong and Echo Beach: the surf heart of the village

  • Pererenan: quieter, with views over the fields

Rental demand is strong all year, which makes Canggu popular with investors.
data.intro: Bali's west coast surf village turned lifestyle hub: rice fields, beach clubs and modern villas between Berawa and Pererenan.

highlights.text: Batu Bolong, Echo Beach and Pererenan are ten minutes apart.
highlights.label: Surf and beaches

highlights.text: High year-round occupancy for well-run villas.
highlights.label: Rental yields

highlights.text: Canggu Community School and several Montessori options.
highlights.label: Schools

data.body:
Green, cultural, calm

Ubud sits among river valleys and terraced rice fields, half an hour inland from the coast. Villas here are about views and privacy: a ridge over the Ayung river, a garden facing the fields.

  • Royal palace, museums and the Saturday art market

  • Wellness retreats and yoga studios

  • Cooler evenings than the coast
data.intro: Bali's cultural heart in the hills of Gianyar: jungle valleys, rice terraces, yoga and a slower, greener way of life.

highlights.text: Homes facing the terraces of Tegallalang and Sayan.
highlights.label: Rice-field views

highlights.text: Temples, dance and craft villages all around.
highlights.label: Culture

highlights.text: Some of the world's best-known retreats.
highlights.label: Wellness

data.body:
Hijau, berbudaya, tenang

Ubud terletak di antara lembah sungai dan sawah berundak, setengah jam dari pantai. Vila di sini mengutamakan pemandangan dan privasi: punggung bukit di atas Sungai Ayung, taman yang menghadap sawah.

  • Puri kerajaan, museum dan pasar seni setiap Sabtu

  • Tempat retret dan studio yoga

  • Malam yang lebih sejuk daripada di pesisir
data.intro: Jantung budaya Bali di perbukitan Gianyar: lembah hutan, sawah berundak, yoga dan cara hidup yang lebih lambat dan hijau.

highlights.text: Rumah menghadap sawah berundak Tegallalang dan Sayan.
highlights.label: Pemandangan sawah

highlights.text: Pura, tari dan desa kerajinan di sekelilingnya.
highlights.label: Budaya

highlights.text: Beberapa tempat retret paling terkenal di dunia.
highlights.label: Kebugaran

data.quote: Sekar found us a house in Kemang within three weeks of landing in Jakarta, and somehow knew which school run would be the shortest. Everything after that was just as calm.
Buying a villa from abroad felt daunting. Rafael explained every ownership option in plain English and the notary process was finished before we flew back for the handover.
We entrusted Lumina with the sale of my parents' heritage home. They treated it with the respect it deserved and found a buyer who loves it as much as we did.
Maarten listened to what we really wanted: quiet, green, and close enough to Ubud for dinner. The land he showed us on the second day is now our home.

en.title: Jakarta prime residential market: Q3 2026 review

data.body:

en.title: Buying property in Bali as a foreigner: a practical guide

seo.title: Buying property in Bali as a foreigner (2026 guide)
seo.description: Leasehold, Hak Pakai or PT PMA: how foreigners can own a home in Bali, explained by Lumina Estates.

data.body:
Indonesian law does not allow foreigners to hold freehold (Hak Milik) title directly, but there are three well-established ways to own a home in Bali.

Your options

  1. Leasehold (Hak Sewa): a long lease, usually 25–30 years with an extension option.

  2. Hak Pakai: a right of use available to foreign residents with a KITAS or KITAP.

  3. PT PMA: a foreign-owned company that can hold Hak Guna Bangunan title.

Before you sign

  • Check the zoning and the building permit (PBG)

  • Use an independent notary (PPAT)

  • Confirm the extension terms of any lease in writing
data.excerpt: Leasehold, Hak Pakai or a PT PMA company? A clear overview of how foreigners can own a home in Bali, and the questions to ask before you sign.

id.title: Membeli properti di Bali sebagai warga asing: panduan praktis

data.body:
Hukum Indonesia tidak mengizinkan warga asing memegang Hak Milik secara langsung, tetapi ada tiga cara yang sudah mapan untuk memiliki rumah di Bali.

Pilihan Anda

  1. Hak Sewa: sewa jangka panjang, biasanya 25–30 tahun dengan opsi perpanjangan.

  2. Hak Pakai: hak guna bagi warga asing yang memiliki KITAS atau KITAP.

  3. PT PMA: perusahaan milik asing yang dapat memegang Hak Guna Bangunan.

Sebelum menandatangani

  • Periksa zonasi dan persetujuan bangunan gedung (PBG)

  • Gunakan notaris (PPAT) yang independen

  • Pastikan syarat perpanjangan sewa secara tertulis
data.excerpt: Hak sewa, Hak Pakai atau PT PMA? Gambaran jelas tentang cara warga asing dapat memiliki rumah di Bali, dan pertanyaan yang perlu diajukan sebelum menandatangani.

en.title: Living in Ubud: a year in the hills

data.body:
Ten years ago I came to Ubud for a fortnight. I am still here, and I still find new paths through the rice fields.

Mornings

The day starts early: offerings on every doorstep, the market at Pasar Ubud, coffee before the heat.

The seasons

From November to March the afternoons bring heavy rain and the valleys turn an impossible green. A good roof and a covered terrace matter more than a big pool.

Three things I wish I had known

  • Choose a home within ten minutes of a main road

  • Visit a plot in the rainy season before you buy

  • Learn some Bahasa Indonesia: it opens every door
data.excerpt: Maarten de Vries on what daily life in Ubud is really like, from the morning market to the rainy-season afternoons.

en.title: Renting a family home in South Jakarta: what to expect

data.body:
Most landlords in Jakarta expect rent to be paid one or two years in advance. That surprises many newcomers, so it is worth planning for early.

The usual terms

  • Minimum lease of one or two years

  • Rent paid in advance, plus a security deposit

  • Landlord responsible for structural repairs; tenant for day-to-day maintenance

Choosing the area

Kemang suits families who like cafés and walking; Pondok Indah offers larger gardens, the golf course and the hospital.

en.title: Five things to check before renewing a villa lease in Bali

data.body:
Many leasehold villas in Bali were built on 25-year leases signed in the early 2000s. Those terms are now ending, and renewal is rarely as simple as a signature.

Check these five points

  1. The exact end date and any notice period in the original lease

  2. Whether the extension price was fixed in advance

  3. Who owns the buildings when the lease ends

  4. Changes in zoning since the villa was built

  5. The landowner family's current heirs and their consent

If in doubt, ask a notary to review the original deed before you open negotiations.
data.excerpt: Lease renewals are where many Bali villa owners lose value. Five points to agree in writing before the current term runs out.
